"'''Another Night'''" is a song by German [[Eurodance]] and [[pop music]] project [[Real McCoy (band)|Real McCoy]] (also known as '''M.C. Sar & The Real McCoy'''). The single is featured on their hit album ''[[Another Night (Real McCoy album)|Another Night]]'' (1995), which was the American release of the project's second album, ''Space Invaders''. The song was written by J. Wind, Quickmix and [[O-Jay|Olaf Jeglitza]] and was produced by Freshline (J. Wind and Quickmix) and the Berman Brothers. It was released in Europe on 12 July 1993, by [[Hansa Records]], and two music videos were produced, directed by [[Nigel Dick]] (US version) and Angel Gracia (European version).

Initially a sleeper hit in Germany in 1993, "Another Night" would go on to reach the top three in the United Kingdom and United States in late 1994. It peaked at number one in Australia, Scotland and Zimbabwe, as well as on the Canadian and US dance charts. In 2008, "Another Night" was ranked at number 91 on ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine's "Top 100 Songs of the First 50 Years of the [[Hot 100]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-00.shtml |title=The Billboard Hot 100 All-Time Top Songs (100-91) |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=4 October 2008 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120722054331/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-00.shtml |archive-date=22 July 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Ten years later, commemorating the 60th anniversary of the Hot 100, "Another Night" ranked at position 117.<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100-60th-anniversary | title=Hot 100 60th Anniversary | magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] }}</ref> In 2025, the magazine ranked it among "The 100 Best Dance Songs of All Time".<ref name="billboard2025">{{cite magazine|first1=Andrea|last1=Domanick|first2=Andrew|last2=Unterberger|first3=Elias|last3=Leight|first4=Eric|last4=Renner Brown|first5=Jason|last5=Lipshutz|first6=Joe|last6=Lynch|first7=Kat|last7=Bein|first8=Katie|last8=Bein|first9=Krystal|last9=Rodriguez|first10=Lily|last10=Moayeri|first11=Melinda|last11=Newman|first12=Thomas|last12=Smith|first13=Zei|last13=McCarthy|url=https://www.billboard.com/lists/best-dance-songs-all-time/|title=The 100 Best Dance Songs of All Time: Staff List|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=28 March 2025|access-date=6 April 2025}}</ref>

The single is featured on their hit album Another Night (1995), which was the American release of the project's second album, Space Invaders. The song was written by J. Wind, Quickmix and Olaf Jeglitza and was produced by Freshline (J. Wind and Quickmix) and the Berman Brothers. It was released in Europe on 12 July 1993, by Hansa Records, and two music videos were produced, directed by Nigel Dick (US version) and Angel Gracia (European version).

Initially a sleeper hit in Germany in 1993, "Another Night" would go on to reach the top three in the United Kingdom and United States in late 1994. It peaked at number one in Australia, Scotland and Zimbabwe, as well as on the Canadian and US dance charts. In 2008, "Another Night" was ranked at number 91 on Billboard magazine's "Top 100 Songs of the First 50 Years of the Hot 100. Ten years later, commemorating the 60th anniversary of the Hot 100, "Another Night" ranked at position 117. In 2025, the magazine ranked it among "The 100 Best Dance Songs of All Time".

sections.heading: Background and release
sections.wikitext:
{{unreferencedsect|date=December 2025}}
"Another Night" was originally released in Europe in the Summer of 1993 through [[Hansa Records]] (BMG Berlin).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Real McCoy and the Secret Behind “Another Night” |url=https://vocal.media/beat/real-mc-coy-and-the-secret-behind-another-night |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=Beat |language=en}}</ref> At first the single was only a minor hit in Europe. It had peaked at No.18 in Germany but had barely managed to make the Top 100 in other countries in Europe. Thanks to the promotional efforts of BMG Canada, the single suddenly reached No.1 on the Canadian charts in the Spring of 1994. The success of the single in Canada caught the attention of [[Arista Records]] CEO [[Clive Davis]] who at the time had become interested in bringing another European music project to the US market after becoming successful with the Swedish pop group [[Ace of Base]]. Once a new deal was finalized between Arista and BMG, the project name was shortened to Real McCoy and an all new release of the single was quickly planned for Summer 1994. Thanks to the promotional efforts of Arista in 1994, "Another Night" quickly reached No.3 on the US charts and remained on the US chart for over 45 weeks.<ref name=":0" /> It was also certified [[RIAA certification|Platinum]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]]. The single also achieved Platinum sales in Australia and Silver status in the United Kingdom.

sections.heading: Composition, vocals, and lyrics
sections.wikitext: While singer Patricia "Patsy" Petersen stars in the music videos for the single, the actual vocals on the track were recorded with studio singer Karin Kasar. German rapper Olaf Jeglitza (O-Jay) wrote and performed the rap vocals on the single. "Another Night" was originally inspired by the [[Roni Griffith]] song "Desire" (1981), the [[Coca-Cola]] theme tune, and the [[Captain Hollywood Project]] song "[[More and More (Captain Hollywood Project song)|More and More]]" (1992). The song lyrics tell the story of a woman who longs to be with the anonymous individual she encounters every night in her dreams. The rap vocals represent the man's voice in the woman's head, saying the things she wants to hear and promising to fulfill her desires and cover her with his love. However, each dawn brings pain to the vocalist, as she realizes: "''When the night is gone, I'll be alone.''"{{fact|date=October 2024}}

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
Upon the release, [[Larry Flick]] from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine described the song as an "instantly infectious and jaunty li'l [[rave music|rave]]/[[hi-NRG|NRG]] jumper that may initially remind some of '[[What Is Love]]' by [[Haddaway]]. A close spin, however, reveals a frothy confection that stands on its own pop merits. Nicely contrasted male/female duet vocals kick lovely, as do peppy remixes [...]. Already wooing folks aboard, single has the strength to keep the glow of summer parties lingering for a long time to come."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1994/BB-1994-07-16.pdf|first=Larry|last=Flick|title=New & Noteworthy|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=16 July 1994|access-date=23 January 2018|author-link=Larry Flick}}</ref> [[David Browne (journalist)|David Browne]] from ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' said it is "a swooshing glop of diva-on-a-downer voice, Eurotrash synths, and rapping."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/article/1995/02/17/current-radio-hits/|first=David|last=Browne|title=Current radio hits|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=17 February 1995|accessdate=23 February 2020|author-link=David Browne (journalist)}}</ref> Dave Sholin from the ''[[Gavin Report]]'' wrote that "those of you into catchy, high-energy, pop creations from groups like the [[Captain Hollywood Project]] or [[Culture Beat]] will love this track."<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Dave |last= Sholin |title= Singles |magazine= [[Gavin Report]] |access-date= 15 April 2018 |url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Gavin-Report/90/94/Gavin-1994-08-12.pdf}}</ref> Rachel Cohen from ''[[The Heights (newspaper)|The Heights]]'' named it the best dance track of the album, along with "[[Run Away (Real McCoy song)|Run Away]]". She described it as "fast-paced and energetic". noting that it has "a distinct beat and sound".<ref>{{cite news|first1= Rachel |last1= Cohen |url= https://newspapers.bc.edu/cgi-bin/bostonsh?a=d&d=bcheights19950403.2.78 |title= Sober forecast for Seattle superband Mad Season |newspaper= [[The Heights (newspaper)|The Heights]] |page= 28 |date= 3 April 1995 |accessdate= 15 April 2020}}</ref> Howard Cohen from ''[[Spartanburg Herald-Journal|Herald-Journal]]'' called it an "infectious tune, bubbling with strobe-like keyboards and melody".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ObQeAAAAIBAJ|first=Howard|last=Cohen|title=Beatles release shows group at working best|magazine=[[Spartanburg Herald-Journal|Herald-Journal]]|date=13 April 1995|accessdate=12 March 2020}}</ref> 

Dennis Hunt from ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' felt it's "awfully catchy".<ref>{{cite news|first=Dennis|last=Hunt|title=In Brief|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=16 April 1995|page=|accessdate=22 January 2023|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1995-04-16-ca-55148-story.html}}</ref> In his weekly UK chart commentary, [[James Masterton]] said, "It stands out in many ways owing to the strange billing the act has."<ref>{{cite web|last=Masterton|first=James|title=Week Ending November 12th 1994|url=https://chart-watch.uk/archives/1994/week-ending-november-12th-1994|website=Chart Watch UK|date=6 November 1994|accessdate=9 September 2021|author-link=James Masterton}}</ref> Alan Jones from ''[[Music Week]]'' gave the song a top score of five out of five, declaring it "a fiendish continental creation that's laid siege to Europe and is climbing the US Top 10." He added further, "A hugely commercial [[Dance-pop|pop/dance]] confection with the usual male rap verse/female sung chorus combination that has proved so popular. File next to [[Whigfield]]."<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Alan |last= Jones |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1994/Music-Week-1994-10-15.pdf |title= Market Preview: Mainstream - Singles |magazine= [[Music Week]] |date= 15 October 1994 |page= 18 |accessdate= 23 April 2021}}</ref> Wendi Cermak from ''The Network Forty'' named it a "great dance record".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Archive-Network-40/94/Network-40-1994-07-08.pdf|first=Wendi|last=Cermak|title=Crossover|magazine=The Network Forty|date=8 July 1994|page=24|access-date=29 March 2020}}</ref> The magazine also compared it to "[[Rhythm Is a Dancer]]" by [[Snap!]]. sections.heading: Chart performance

"Another Night" debuted on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] at number 77 on the week ending 27 August 1994.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/1994-08-27 |title=Music: Top 100 Songs - Billboard Hot 100 Chart |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=8 May 2016}}</ref> On the week ending 12 November 1994, the single reached its peak position of number three.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aAgEAAAAMBAJ |title=Billboard (November 12, 1994 Issue) - Google Books |date=12 November 1994 |access-date=8 May 2016}}</ref><ref name="Hot100Peak">{{cite magazine | url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/1994-11-12/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141120003232/https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/1994-11-12/ | archive-date=20 November 2014 | title=Billboard Hot 100 - Billboard - Week of November 12, 1994 | magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] | date=12 November 1994 | access-date=13 December 2023 | url-status=live}}</ref> The song also brought the group the distinction of having the longest run at number three, at 11 non-consecutive weeks.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Brandy's 'Baby' Grows Up Fast|last=Bronson|first=Fred|author-link=Fred Bronson|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|volume=107|issue=6|page=96|date=11 February 1995}}</ref> It stayed on the chart for 45 weeks.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/artist/418947/real-mccoy/chart |title=The Real McCoy - Chart History |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |accessdate=8 May 2016}}</ref> By the end of 1994, the single had sold approximately 700,000 copies in the US according to [[Nielsen Soundscan]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uAsEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA57 |title=Best-Selling Records of 1994 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=21 January 1995 |access-date=18 December 2020 |page=57 |issn=0006-2510|volume=107|number=3}}</ref>

sections.text:
"Another Night" debuted on the US Billboard Hot 100 at number 77 on the week ending 27 August 1994. On the week ending 12 November 1994, the single reached its peak position of number three. The song also brought the group the distinction of having the longest run at number three, at 11 non-consecutive weeks. It stayed on the chart for 45 weeks. By the end of 1994, the single had sold approximately 700,000 copies in the US according to Nielsen Soundscan.

In Europe, "Another Night" was a number-one hit in Scotland and entered the top 10 in Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Ireland, Norway, and the United Kingdom, as well as on the Eurochart Hot 100, where it peaked at number 10 on 26 November 1994. It debuted on the chart at number 87 on 2 October 1993, after charting in Germany and Switzerland. On the European Dance Radio Chart, it peaked at number five the same week. In the United Kingdom, it reached number two during its fourth week on the UK Singles Chart, on 13 November 1994. It stayed within the UK top 100 for a total of 19 weeks. Additionally, "Another Night" was a top-20 hit in France, Germany, Iceland and the Netherlands. In Australia and Zimbabwe, it peaked at number one for six and two weeks, respectively, as well as on the Canadian RPM Dance/Urban chart and the US Billboard Dance Club Play chart. "Another Night" earned a gold record in New Zealand, a silver record in the UK and a platinum record in both Australia and the US.

In 2017, to mark the 25th anniversary of the Pop Songs chart, Billboard magazine released a list of the 100 best-performing pop airplay songs since the chart's beginning in 1992. "Another Night" topped the list.
